editorial.description_en: A white with the faint warmth of the inside of a shell — a step deeper and a step more yellow than thin paper.
editorial.description_ja: 貝の内側のような、やわらかい温かみのある白。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.944, C 0.011, h 76.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 貝 (kai, shell) + 白 (shiro, white), rendaku to -jiro. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Shell White" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 貝白. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — usu-gami at ΔE00 2.3, asa-nuno at ΔE00 3.4, sekkai-kabe at ΔE00 4.9. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.011 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
